What is driving urchind densities (plot level)? 

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

#read libraries 
```{r}
library(lme4)
library(corrplot)
library(glmmTMB)
library(DHARMa)

```

#Read in data 
```{r}
transects <- read.csv("/Users/tessarehill/Dropbox/MSc/Exclosures/processed_data/cleaned_monitoring_transects.csv")

plots <- read.csv("/Users/tessarehill/Dropbox/MSc/Exclosures/processed_data/cleaned_data.csv")
```

#Formatting 
```{r}
plots_glm <- plots

#log transform urchin density data (need to add a small constant because of zero values)
plots_glm$log_urchin_density <- log(plots_glm$urchin_density + 1)

#inspecting urchin distributions (to verify assumptions of fitting a GLMM)
hist(plots_glm$log_urchin_density, main = "Histogram of (log) Urchin Density", xlab = "Urchin Density")

#shapiro-Wilk test for normality, p less than 0.05, normally distributed
shapiro.test(plots_glm$log_urchin_density) #normally distributed 
shapiro.test(plots_glm$urchin_density) #normally distributed

#check for overdispersion -log 
mean_density <- mean(plots_glm$log_urchin_density, na.rm = TRUE)
var_density <- var(plots_glm$log_urchin_density, na.rm = TRUE)
overdispersion <- var_density / mean_density #0.653 (oof), close to 1 is good 
print(overdispersion)  #0.65 = overdispersion - variance is greater than mean 

#check for overdispersion 
mean_density <- mean(plots_glm$urchin_density, na.rm = TRUE)
var_density <- var(plots_glm$urchin_density, na.rm = TRUE)
overdispersion <- var_density / mean_density #0.653 (oof), close to 1 is good 
print(overdispersion)  #2.45 = overdispersion

#variance > mean - GP, NB or CMP GLMs 

#check for over zero inflation 
sum(plots_glm$log_urchin_density == 0, na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(plots) #a lot of zeros (39%), indicated zero-inflated 

#convert month to numeric 
plots_glm$month <- as.factor(plots_glm$month)
plots_glm$month <- as.numeric(plots_glm$month)

colnames(plots_glm) #check numerical predictors 

#correlation matrix of environmental variables 
cor_matrix <- cor(plots_glm[, c("mean_light_lux", "mean_temperature_c", "bottom_salinity", "bottom_ph", "mean_depth_m", "bottom_temp", "bottom_do", "month", "species_richness", "shannon_div", "simp_div", "kelp_survival", "kelp_growth", "site_density")], use = "complete.obs")

print(cor_matrix)

#visualize with a heatmap 
corrplot(cor_matrix, method = "circle")

#VIF factor - VIF quantifies how much the variance of a predictor is inflated due to multicollinearity. High VIF values (>5 or 10) indicate problematic collinearity. 

#with all predictors 
lm_model <- lm(log_urchin_density ~ mean_light_lux + mean_temperature_c + bottom_salinity + bottom_ph +
               mean_depth_m + bottom_temp + bottom_do + month + species_richness + 
               shannon_div + simp_div + kelp_growth + site_density + kelp_survival, data = plots_glm)

vif(lm_model) #so many >5

#check vif of predictors we will use in our model
#removed ph, salinity, and bottom_temp
lm_model <- lm(log_urchin_density ~ mean_light_lux + mean_temperature_c +
               mean_depth_m  + bottom_do + month  + kelp_survival + site_density, data = plots_glm)

vif(lm_model)

#check for NA 
summary(plots_glm)
colnames(plots_glm)

#standardizing predictors
plots_glm$mean_temperature_c <- scale(plots_glm$mean_temperature_c)
plots_glm$bottom_do <- scale(plots_glm$bottom_do)
plots_glm$mean_light_lux <- scale(plots_glm$mean_light_lux)
plots_glm$mean_depth_m <- scale(plots_glm$mean_depth_m)
plots_glm$month <- scale(plots_glm$month)
plots_glm$site_density <- scale(plots_glm$site_density)
plots_glm$simp_div <- scale(plots_glm$simp_div)

#month needs to be turned back into a factor
plots_glm$month <- factor(plots_glm$month)
plots_glm$treatment <- as.factor(plots_glm$treatment)


```

Zero Inflated Negative Binomial GLMM
```{r}
#response variable as integer 
plots_glm$log_urchin_density <- as.integer(plots_glm$log_urchin_density)
plots_glm$urchin_density <- as.integer(plots_glm$urchin_density)

#include ALL predictors in first model 
model1 <- glmmTMB(urchin_density ~ treatment + mean_temperature_c  + bottom_do + (1 | site),
                  zi = ~ treatment +  mean_temperature_c  + bottom_do,
                  family = nbinom2, 
                  data = plots_glm)

summary(model1)
AIC(model1) 




```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
